Derive major-cluster parentage from a vector of set ids.

Source: R/ceLLMarkup.R
dot-cv_cellmarkup_parentage.Rd

Returns a named character vector, one entry per id, holding that id's parent or `NA` when it has none. A set `P` is the parent of `S` when `S` begins with `paste0(P, "-")` and `P` is itself one of the ids. The LONGEST candidate wins, so a cluster called `"C1"` cannot claim `"C10-Sub1"` – which a `"-Sub[0-9]+$"` pattern would also get right, but only by accident of the naming, whereas matching against the real ids is exact.

Usage

.cv_cellmarkup_parentage(set_names, enabled = TRUE)

Details

Both levels have to be present. A call carrying only sub-clusters has no parent identity available to inherit, so every entry comes back `NA` and the caller takes its ordinary single-request path.
